matches.title: Crystal Palace vs Everton
matches.description: Watch Crystal Palace vs Everton highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 10, 2026. The stage was set for a classic Premier League encounter as Crystal Palace hosted Everton in a match that promised intensity and tactical drama. With 24,958 fans in attendance, the atmosphere reflected the high stakes of a mid-May battle for positioning in the world's most competitive league. Toffees Strike Early, Eagles Respond The match, held on May 10, 2026 , burst into life within the opening minutes. Everton wasted no time establishing their physical presence, and in the 6th minute, they found the breakthrough. Following a period of sustained pressure from set-pieces, James Tarkowski reacted quickest in the box to slot the ball home with his right foot. The early setback forced Crystal Palace to sharpen their focus, as they began to dominate possession and search for a gap in the organized Everton defense. Their persistence was rewarded in the 34th minute. Ismaila Sarr showcased his clinical edge, picking up a loose ball and firing a left-footed strike past Jordan Pickford to level the scores. The first half ended with a flurry of tactical fouls and yellow cards for James Garner and Vitaliy Mykolenko , signaling the growing tension between the two sides. Second Half Shifts and Late Drama The second half followed a similar script to the first, with Everton regaining the lead almost immediately after the restart. In the 47th minute, provider turned goalscorer as James Tarkowski delivered an assist for Beto , who finished emphatically with his right foot. Facing another deficit, Crystal Palace turned to their bench, introducing Jean-Philippe Mateta in the 65th minute to provide a fresh attacking impetus. Mateta’s impact was instantaneous. In the 77th minute, the French striker found space in the danger zone and unleashed a left-footed shot that drew the hosts level once more. The final stages were dominated by the Eagles , who pushed for a winner with 59% of the total possession. Mateta nearly turned hero in stoppage time but sent a golden opportunity wide, and a late block on Carlos Alcaraz 's goal-bound effort ensured both teams walked away with a hard-earned point.

The atmosphere at Goodison Park was charged with anticipation as both sides locked horns in a pivotal Premier League encounter held on May 4, 2026. Establishing the tempo Manchester City controlled the early proceedings, moving the ball with purpose and probing for openings. Their persistence was rewarded in the 43rd minute when Jeremy Doku clinicaly converted a pass from Bernardo Silva , with Rayan Cherki providing the assist. This opener gave the visitors a deserved lead as they headed into the break, feeling comfortable despite the occasional defensive scramble. The Toffees strike back The second half transformed into a chaotic affair as the hosts surged forward with newfound confidence. Thierno Barry capitalized on a loose ball in the 68th minute to level the playing field. The momentum shifted entirely to the home side when Jake O'Brien powered home a header from a James Garner corner in the 73rd minute. The incredible turnaround continued at the 81st minute mark, with Thierno Barry once again in the right place to put the ball away, leaving the visitors stunned. A dramatic conclusion The visitors responded with urgency to salvage their campaign. Erling Haaland produced an excellent lob in the 83rd minute to narrow the gap. In the dying moments of the match, the pressure finally paid off: deep into stoppage time at the 90+7' mark, Jeremy Doku fired home a right-footed strike from outside the box following a Marc Guehi assist, capping off a spectacular match that ended in a dramatic 3-3 draw.

matches.title: Tottenham Hotspur vs Everton
matches.description: Watch Tottenham vs Everton highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 24, 2026. The Premier League season reached a fever pitch on 2026-05-24 as Tottenham Hotspur and Everton locked horns in a tactical battle at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium . Both sides entered the fray looking to secure vital points in a match that promised intensity from the opening whistle. Tight Opening and the Breakthrough The match began with both teams testing each other's defensive organization. Everton looked to utilize set-pieces early on through Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall , while Mathys Tel provided the spark for Tottenham with several dangerous corners. The physical nature of the contest was evident when Jake O'Brien was cautioned early for a cynical pull on his opponent. As the first half progressed, the tension grew until the 43rd minute when the deadlock was finally broken. After a corner from Mathys Tel , the ball fell loose in the box, and Joao Palhinha reacted fastest to slot it home with his left foot, giving the hosts a precious lead going into the interval. Second Half Pressure and VAR Controversy Coming out for the second half, Tottenham looked to double their advantage. Richarlison and Kevin Danso both had significant heading opportunities that went wide or were blocked by a resilient Everton defense. The game took a dramatic turn in the 80th minute when Pape Sarr went down in the box. While the home crowd roared for a penalty, the referee deemed it a dive and booked the midfielder instead, a decision that sparked heated debate across the stadium. This moment of controversy injected fresh energy into the match as both managers turned to their benches, with James Maddison and Randal Kolo Muani entering for the hosts, while Beto and Carlos Alcaraz were introduced for the visitors. A Frantic Finish The closing stages were a test of nerves for Tottenham . Everton threw everything forward, earning a succession of corners delivered by James Garner . In the dying moments, the Toffees nearly found an equalizer when James Tarkowski met a cross, but his header drifted agonizingly wide. Goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky was forced into a crucial late save to preserve the lead, even earning a yellow card for time-wasting in the process. Despite late clearances from Radu Dragusin and Micky van de Ven , the pressure was relentless until the final whistle confirmed a hard-fought victory for the London side, with Joao Palhinha standing out as a Man of the Match contender.
